sources.headline: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang
sources.text: "The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a Tuesday call with financial analysts. The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period.Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter. Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance. Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worry that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader."The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment."Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout happening throughout the technology industry."It is business as usual," she said of what is happening inside of Nvidia now. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us."She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects"."Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this."Despite board chairman Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analyst questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement. Jones said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection."With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new CEO will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."

Nvidia board rules that co-founder Jensen Huang will not return as CEO

Nvidia's board chairman ruled out bringing back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Tuesday, as the chipmaker forecast stronger-than-expected quarterly sales but faced growing questions over its leadership, national security exposure and long-term strategy following his abrupt departure.

Issued on: 17/11/2026 - 23:50

3 min
Reading time
Share
By:
FRANCE 24
FILE PHOTO: Jensen Huang, Founder, President and CEO of NVIDIA, reacts during the Milken Institute Global Conference 2026 in Beverly Hills, California, on May, 4, 2026. © Mike Blake, Reuters

Nvidia Board Chairman Harvey Jones opened a conference call with investors on Tuesday by saying the AI chip company would not rehire co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO and would not take questions on the matter.

Jones' start to a call about quarterly results was a forceful response to a movement to bring back Huang, who stepped down last week. With Huang gone, investors are eager for clues about Nvidia's future and strategy, from its commitments of billions of dollars to cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Shares of the company rose 2% in extended trading, after Nvidia forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets.

"It's no surprise that they're doing very well, and there'll be people who will breathe a sigh of relief about it," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments. "But the story here is very complicated, and it's hard not to factor that in as an additional risk for people buying stock."

Jones said the board had hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new CEO.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also finance chief, kept her focus on financials and products in the statement accompanying results. "Our momentum is real," she said, without addressing the leadership issue. "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track," she added, referring to the company's latest flagship AI chip.

Huang, the AI boom's most prolific salesman, resigned on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Jensen Huang's exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

Fourth-quarter outlook tops targets

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts' average estimate of $125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-centre chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72%, compared with analysts' estimate of 71.7%.

Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said Nvidia's outlook was "quite positive, albeit not as ambitious as in previous quarters, which many have already anticipated." He added, "I don't think anything near-term will be affected by Jensen's departure. His executive leadership team is capable and has followed his leadership and executed effectively for years, reaching this point."

The board is considering internal and external candidates for CEO, with Kress seen offering steady leadership during the selection process. But a growing "Stand With Jensen" campaign has complicated the search, and Huang said on Tuesday he would be "honoured" to return if the board deemed it best.

READ MORE
Nvidia's Jensen Huang: Targeted by the AI misinformation he helped create

National security scrutiny intensifies

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia's board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang's departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker's national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centres serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections fuelled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-centre expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia's next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

READ MORE
Musk, Uber co-founder join calls to reinstate Huang as Nvidia chief

Tuesday's results offer a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia's newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell. Nvidia said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-centre revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.84 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $109.11 billion. The company has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating analysts' estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps.

(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)

Transcript
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day. Today's top stories A technology issue with United Airlines delayed departing flights yesterday evening, just as air travel was returning to normal after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday. President Trump said yesterday that he hopes this incident will prompt Congress to allocate more funds to upgrade the outdated air traffic control system.

🎧 Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the FAA will reevaluate future maintenance procedures, NPR's Joe Hernandez tells Up First. Mike McCormick, a former FAA senior executive and air traffic manager, told Hernandez that he thinks another nationwide ground stop is unlikely. McCormick says that in cases like this, the FAA sometimes imposes a maintenance moratorium, temporarily halting such work. The ground stop happened while L3Harris workers converted copper wires to a fiber optic system and installed a new router in El Dorado, Arkansas. President Trump is in Manila today to meet with allies at the ASEAN summit. Tomorrow, he travels to Shenzhen, China, for a joint summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. It's the first time those three have had a joint summit. The meeting will happen on the sidelines of the APEC summit that Xi is hosting in Shenzhen.
🎧 When leaving the White House yesterday, Trump said they would discuss his "favorite subject": Ukraine, NPR's Deepa Shivaram says. The White House had previously announced that Ukraine would not be on the agenda for the trilateral meeting. Shivaram says that Europe and Ukraine are concerned about how Ukraine may be discussed at the meeting, and what might come out of it, because President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will not be at APEC and Trump has recently been more lenient toward Putin and Russia. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation has shaken Silicon Valley, prompting calls from some tech leaders for the board to reinstate him. Trump said he agreed with them. Meanwhile, the U.S. government introduced a rule to block remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, closing a loophole that could allow adversarial governments to access American AI technology through overseas data centers. Nvidia is the world's dominant producer of AI chips. 🎧 Many prominent AI and venture capital figures have recognized Huang as a visionary whose company played a significant role in the AI boom, NPR's Shannon Bond says. An online petition supporting his reinstatement has garnered more than 160,000 signatures, but Bond says some of them may not be real. Elon Musk says he signed it. Brad Gerstner from Altimeter Capital, a key Nvidia investor, has urged the board to thoroughly investigate and keep all options open. Bond says the interim CEO and CFO will address the public for the first time following today's earnings report.
Prosecutors are moving to retry Lindsay Clancy for the deaths of her three children. The new trial is set for March 29, 2027. Although there was speculation about potentially reducing the charges to manslaughter or second-degree murder after her previous trial ended in a mistrial, no changes were made during Monday's court hearing. Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the first trial, will oversee the new proceedings. He denied Clancy's defense team's request to dismiss the charges based on double jeopardy. Clancy's defense argues that she shouldn't be held criminally responsible for killing her children because she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis. Deep dive

One year ago, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to all families regardless of income, as long as adults are working, seeking work, in school, or unable to work. Many parents have found this initiative life-changing, but capacity was limited. Only 50% of the some 67,000 children ages 5 and under are enrolled in the universal childcare program. Some of the remaining families participate in other programs, such as PreK and Head Start. New Mexico officials say the program must expand to meet demand. The issues observed in New Mexico are mirrored across the nation, prompting policymakers and childcare advocates to closely monitor the state's initiative. 👶 Almost half of U.S. children aged 5 and under live in licensed childcare deserts, where demand exceeds availability, according to the Center for American Progress, a left-leaning think tank.👶 New Mexico's program has an operating budget of nearly $600 million, but some lawmakers are concerned it could be $50 million over budget this year.👶 New Mexico state Sen. Steve Lanier tells NPR that the steep cost of the program is why he only supports universal childcare for some people, since someone earning around $450,000 or $600,000 might not need assistance. Lanier has previously sued to end the initiative, but the lawsuit was unsuccessful.👶 Since the enactment of free, universal childcare in New Mexico, lower-income mothers have experienced significant gains. Their full-time employment has risen by 23%, according to a new paper from Arizona State University.

Millions of shorebirds embark on epic migrations to Alaska each year to breed. They often travel thousands of miles from places like New Zealand, Asia and South America. But researchers have found a concerning trend: Nearly half of the 41 shorebird species that breed in Alaska are in decline. These birds time their journeys to coincide with peak insect availability, and climate change is throwing off their schedules. Warmer springs lead to earlier insect emergence, creating a mismatch that could leave shorebirds without enough food supply. Published: 6:47am, 18 Nov 2026

US chip giant Nvidia doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than US$115 billion, the company reported on Tuesday while ruling out any return for ousted CEO Jensen Huang after a Chinese spy scandal.

The results, which beat expectations, came hours after Huang said he wanted his job back in the latest twist for the company at the centre of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

Huang, a leading promoter of AI, stepped down last week following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a spy for Beijing.

Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” interim CEO Colette Kress said in a statement, her first since being appointed by the board last week.

Nvidia’s Colette Kress poses for a photo. Photo: Nvidia via Reuters

She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 per cent in next financial year, up from 70 per cent.

The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia – which has lost US$700 billion in market value since the scandal broke – and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

But his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even US President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in his first statement since his resignation.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

But Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, slapped down the move, saying in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”.

05:21
The rise and fall of Jensen Huang, who has resigned as Nvidia’s CEO

As the scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil – countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed – a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

Investors will be watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying: “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.”
